question: What is the maximum strength of members in a State Legislative Assembly as per the Constitution of India?
solution: The correct answer is __**500**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ • The **Constitution of India**, under **Article 170**, specifies the maximum strength of the Legislative Assembly of a state to be **500 members** and the minimum strength to be **60 members**. • The strength of the Legislative Assembly varies from state to state based on the population of the state. For example, Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Assembly with **403 members**. • However, there are exceptions to the minimum strength of 60 members. States like **Sikkim (32 members), Mizoram (40 members), and Goa (40 members)** have fewer members in their Legislative Assembly. • The members of the Legislative Assembly are directly elected by the people of the respective states through a democratic electoral process. • Each member represents a specific constituency within the state, and elections are held using the **first-past-the-post system**.
